paragraphs.text: In the wettest part of north-east India, wooden bridges rot within a few years. Villages there guide the roots of fig trees across streams instead, building bridges that are alive and grow stronger each season.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: A root bridge takes fifteen to thirty years to become usable. The roots are trained along a frame of bamboo, which rots away once the roots have crossed and thickened enough to carry weight.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Engineers have measured several of them. The oldest carry more than fifty people at once, and unlike concrete they repair themselves after floods, though they cannot be built where the water is too wide.
paragraphs.label: C
